label: EXPLORATORY
rule: QUESTIONS are drawn, not events, so every sampled panel is complete (all its changed answers are judged) and the gated panel can be simulated. ``n_questions`` = round(400 / (helpful+harmful events per question in the population)), drawn by numpy.random.default_rng(seed).permutation over the sorted question ids; every changed answer of every source on a drawn question is included. The thinking subsample: the drawn questions in a second permutation (seed + 1), taken in order until they hold at least ``thinking_events`` events (counts of events only). Selection never reads a judge output, and no per-question outcome is used.
deviation: questions (complete panels) are sampled rather than ~400 helpful/harmful + ~100 wrong->wrong events, so the gated panel can be simulated; wrong->wrong events are therefore ~250, not ~100
limitation_identifiable_revision: share of responses mentioning panel/peer/member: revised 0.984, original 0.009: without labels the revision is still usually identifiable from its content
